![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14075482/assets/8ce943f8a77fe5756fdaf77185d8b59493ef0da95da3605f1f2416786f9ec394.png)

Find the global extrema of the function $f(x,y)=xy-4$ on the closed region $D={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le x\le 2,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le 4},$ shown above.
worked_solution:
Since $f(x,y)$ is continuous on the closed, bounded region $D,$ the function attains a global maximum and minimum on $D.$

To find the extreme values, we follow three steps.

**Step 1.** Find the critical points of $f$ inside the region. 

To determine the critical points, we solve ${f}^{′}=0.$ Computing the derivative gives

$$
{f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}y,\,x\end{aligned}].
$$

The derivative exists at each point inside $D,$ and it equals zero when

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0,\,y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us a single point $(0,0).$ Since the point $(0,0)$ does not belong to the interior of $D,$ we do not yet include it in the list of candidates for extrema (it lies on the boundary of $D,$ so we will consider it in the next step).

**Step 2.**  Find the points on the boundary of $D$ that could give rise to extreme values. 

To find the points on the boundary that could give rise to extreme values, we parametrize each part of the boundary:

- The line connecting $(-2,4)$ and $(2,4)$ can be parametrized as

$$
r=⟨t,4⟩,\,t\in (-2,2).
$$

The values of $f$ on this boundary are given by the function

$$
\begin{aligned}F(t) & =f(x(t),y(t)) \\  & =f(t,4) \\  & =(t)(4)-4 \\  & =4t-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the derivative of $F(t)$ is constant. So, $F(t)$ does not have critical points in the open interval $t\in (-2,2).$

- The parabola connecting $(-2,4)$ and $(2,4)$ can be parametrized as

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =⟨t,{t}^{2}⟩,\,t\in (-2,2).\end{aligned}
$$

The values of $f$ on the boundary are given by the function

$$
\begin{aligned}F(t) & =f(x(t),y(t)) \\  & =f(t,{t}^{2}) \\  & =(t)({t}^{2})-4 \\  & ={t}^{3}-4.\end{aligned}
$$

 
To find the critical points of $F(t)$ on the open interval $t\in (-2,2),$ we solve the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{F}^{′}(t) & =0 \\ ({t}^{3}-4)^{′} & =0 \\ 3{t}^{2} & =0 \\ t & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The final equation gives one solution $t=0$ inside the interval $t\in (-2,2).$
Evaluating the corresponding values of $x$ and $y$ on the boundary, we obtain one candidate point, $(0,0).$

Also, we have to include the corner points of the region as candidates for extrema. So, in total we obtain three candidates:

$$
(0,0),\,(2,4),\,(-2,4)
$$

**Step 3.** Evaluate $f(x,y)$ at each of the candidate points, and compare their values. 

Evaluating $f(x,y)$ at each of the points mentioned above, we get the following: 

| $(x,y)$ | $(0,0)$ | $(2,4)$ | $(-2,4)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x,y)$ | $-4$ | $4$ | $-12$ |

Therefore, on the closed region $D,$ we have that 

- $f$ attains the global minimum of $-12$ at the point $(-2,4)$ and

- $f$ attains the global maximum of $4$ at the points $(2,4).$
